changes.after: An interface lets different classes provide the same named action in their own way.

before: An interface specifies operations that implementing classes must provide, and may provide default implementations. Implementing an interface uses a colon and its name without a constructor call.

The function show accepts any Formatter, not just Plain. A class implementing the contract must mark its implementation override. The expression-bodied syntax = expression returns the expression’s value.
Expected output or behavior: C. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
Optional local transfer task: Add another formatter without changing show. You may trace it without a Kotlin compiler; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: An interface describes actions an object must support. This is its contract, or promise to other code. Formatter promises a format function that takes text and returns text. An interface may also supply default function bodies.

A class implements an interface by providing its required actions. Plain and Marked both use `override` for format. The show function accepts any Formatter, so it can use either class without changing its own code.
The screen shows `C`. The object passed to show is a Plain, whose format function returns the text unchanged.
A Marked object follows the same interface but puts brackets around the text. The interface fixes the action's name and input and result types; each class supplies the behavior.
